sections.overall: It's not uncommon for the post PPV to be quiet in terms of the rankings! The average loss per wreslter competed was 0.2, with the range of changes from -1.94 to 2.22. The top match of the week was MJF vs Mark Briscoe (8.08), the opener on a generally well-received Dynamite.
sections.mens: As well as the afore-mentioned Men's World Title match, Kyle Fletcher vs El Phantasmo (7.57) was a decent main event on Collision, though far from the lofty heights we've become accustomed to Fletcher singles matches. The only other match that broke the '7' barrier was Andrade El Idolo vs Brian Cage. It will be exciting to see how Andrade is booked, now that he is a 'face' for the first time in AEW.
sections.womens: In all honesty, the 'Survival of the Fittest' match for the TBS title was a let down. Still, let's hope that Hikaru Shida, the new champ, gets opportunities for decent matches and feuds. Athena's match against the debuting Rina was the best women's match of the week (7.3). Also, welcome back to Kris Statlander - back in at #4 after her brief hiatus from the rankings.
sections.menstag: No standout matches this week and to be honest, one would expect more from Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay in their match against The Swirl (6.18). Each of these stars' ratings took a slight hit as a result. Castagnoli & PAC return to the rankings this week, one of many Death Rider combinations in the Tag and Trios divisions.
sections.womenstag: No matches this week. Although the Divine Dominion promos are always entertaining at least!
sections.trios: The Rascalz starred in their match against the unique combination of Bailey, Bandido & Mistico on Collision (6.79). No major changes in the division this week.
